justification: Attack targets what agents write to and carry across sessions in sliding-window and RAG memory; persistence and unauthorized-action rates measured on representative agent setups in the lab.

Contribution is a prompt-based confidence/uncertainty signal deciding when the agent must defer and ask for clarification; validated in the lab on WebShop, ALFWorld and REAL variants across five backbones.

Headline artefact is MAFBench, an instrument plus taxonomy for measuring multi-agent framework behaviour; evidence is a lab study under controlled framework-level conditions isolating architectural effects.
STRIDE decides whether an agentic loop is warranted at all versus a single LLM call; assessed on 30 real SRE/compliance/enterprise tasks with six months of expert validation in those working domains.

Runtime decides how many LLM calls the pipeline spends, merging agents under a quality floor for token savings; evidence is lab comparisons against LangGraph, DSPy and a hand-tuned oracle across modes.
Contribution routes subtasks to third-party specialist agents via skill discovery and an inter-agent protocol; validated in the lab through 239 simulations and 240 LLM tasks, not a deployed market.
Proposes BOLAA, a controller orchestrating labour agents and their communication; validated by lab simulations in decision-making and reasoning environments. Runner-up: loop_evaluation_and_diagnosis.

Studies which inter-agent communication strategies work under information asymmetry, with an environment verifier as a second factor; lab experiments on an extended Einstein Puzzles game, not real use.
Attack forces repetitive or irrelevant actions and the paper's mechanism claim is that self-examination detection fails to catch it; lab evaluations vary attack methods, surfaces and properties.
The controller checks preconditions and authorizes execution before tools are used, a pre-execution gate; validated in the lab over 360 episodes against ReAct and LangChain baselines.

Paper states it distinguishes itself by an integrated monitoring system combining internal reasoning and execution results to detect failures; evaluated on task scenarios against existing methods, not in production.
Contribution is agent-controlled consolidation and pruning of interaction history to fight context bloat; validated on five SWE-bench Lite instances with token and accuracy measurements.

Proposes run-time attestation, audit agents verifying intent versus behaviour, and challenge-response gating for high-risk operations; OPERA is described as designed to measure, with no results reported.

Object is the feedback that drives rewriting: output-only human feedback cannot identify root causes, a feedback-quality bottleneck; lab study varying instruction granularity plus a diagnostic intervention.
Task Memory Tree keeps step state outside the prompt and prompts are synthesised from the active node path; validated by case studies and comparative lab experiments on multi-step tasks.

Contribution distils reusable skills from the agent's own traces and patches them; the headline evidence removes prune patches to attribute quality effects on held-out SpreadsheetBench and SkillsBench tasks.
Synthesises 22 intrinsic properties over six lifecycle layers into an Entropy Principle framing of silent failure, a conceptual structuring of the field rather than a tested mechanism.

Contribution is broadening exploration of the solution space by running many agents in parallel under a shared leaderboard reward; backed by case-study evidence on one product-to-catalog matching testbed.

Outer loop co-evolves the policy and the training harness across episodes, accumulating reusable skills; validated on math, competitive programming and repo-level SWE against human-engineered RL references.

Title records a MAPE control loop applied to continuous improvement of a deployed AI agent from usage data; EACL Industry Track reporting the flywheel in real operation. Title-only record, low confidence.

Agents may only emit actions from finite catalogs enforced at the tool-output interface, a policy-bounded gate certified in Lean 4; evaluated in the lab on 282 attack graphs and 80 runs across temperatures.

Formalises the agent as a closed loop of structured planning, probe monitoring and event-based orchestration that fixes step order; support is an architecture argument plus a reference implementation demonstration.

Contribution arranges agents for decentralized resilience via gossip dissemination, computational trust and federated adaptation; empirical lab comparison against state-of-the-art multi-agent baselines.

An evolution module beside the BDI reasoning loop rewrites goals and synthesises new code between episodes; evidence is a prototype demonstration in a dynamic multi-agent environment, no measurements.
Semantic Kinematics adds a PID/EKF inner loop that chooses each next step without invoking the LLM; validated on a Wikipedia navigation benchmark against Chain-of-Thought agents.
